title: Video game sales that level off

stimulus.title: Total sales of a video game
stimulus.text: A video game studio tracks the total number of copies of a new game sold since its release. The table gives the total sales $S$, in thousands of copies, $t$ weeks after release. The total sales are modeled by the function $S(t) = a + b\ln t$, whose graph passes through both data points.

table.caption: Total sales S, in thousands of copies, t weeks after release

parts.label: A(i)
parts.prompt: Use the given data to write two equations that can be used to find the values of the constants $a$ and $b$ in the expression for $S(t)$.

rubric.point: Two correct equations, one for each data point

parts.label: A(ii)
parts.prompt: Find the values of $a$ and $b$ as decimal approximations.
parts.sample: $\ln 1 = 0$, so $a = 12$. Then $b\ln 8 = 25$, so $b = \frac{25}{\ln 8} \approx 12.022$ (stored, not rounded, for later parts).

parts.label: B(i)
parts.prompt: Use the given data to find the average rate of change of $S$, in thousands of copies per week, from $t = 1$ to $t = 8$. Express your answer as a decimal approximation. Show the computations that lead to your answer.

rubric.point: The difference quotient from the data, about $3.571$ thousand copies per week

parts.sample: $\frac{S(8) - S(1)}{8 - 1} = \frac{37 - 12}{7} = \frac{25}{7} \approx 3.571$ thousand copies per week, the slope of the secant line through $(1, 12)$ and $(8, 37)$.

parts.label: B(ii)
parts.prompt: Use the average rate of change from part B(i) to estimate the total sales at $t = 4$. Is this estimate an overestimate or an underestimate of the value of the model $S(4)$? Explain your reasoning using the concavity of the graph of $S$.

rubric.point: The estimate $12 + 3 \cdot \frac{25}{7} \approx 22.714$ on the secant line, and "underestimate" because $S$ is concave down on $[1, 8]$, so its graph lies above the secant line
accept: $\approx 22.714$; underestimate, since $b > 0$ makes $S$ concave down on $[1, 8]$ and the secant line lies below the graph
the rate of change of $S$ is decreasing on $[1, 8]$, so the secant lies below the graph there

parts.sample: Using the secant line through $(1, 12)$: $12 + \frac{25}{7}(4 - 1) \approx 22.714$ thousand copies. $S(t) = 12 + b\ln t$ with $b > 0$ is concave down on $[1, 8]$, so the graph of $S$ lies above the secant line on that interval and the estimate is an underestimate. (Indeed $S(4) \approx 28.667$.)

parts.label: C(i)
parts.prompt: According to the model, when will the total sales reach $60$ thousand copies? Give your answer correct to three decimal places.
parts.sample: Solve $12 + b\ln t = 60$: $\ln t = \frac{48}{b}$, so $t = e^{48/b} \approx 54.192$ weeks.

parts.label: C(ii)
parts.prompt: The studio expects sales of the game to level off after a few months, as most interested players have bought it. Explain why the model's error is likely to grow for values of $t$ greater than $8$, and what that means for the answer to part C(i).

rubric.point: The data stop at $t = 8$, so the model is unsupported after that; the model keeps increasing without bound while actual sales level off, so the model overestimates more and more, and $60$ thousand may come later or never
accept: The model is fit to data only up to $8$ weeks; $\lim_{t \to \infty} S(t) = \infty$ but real sales level off, so the gap between model and actual sales grows and the predicted time of about $54$ weeks is too early

parts.sample: The model was built from data with $1 \le t \le 8$, so past week $8$ no data support it. $S(t)$ keeps increasing without bound, $\lim_{t \to \infty} S(t) = \infty$, while actual sales level off. So the model's predictions get further above the actual sales as $t$ increases, and the time of about 54.2 weeks from part C(i) is likely too early: actual sales may reach $60$ thousand much later, or not at all.
